title: PET and MRI learning classifies prostate lesion risk
summary: An ensemble of random forests combined PSMA PET and MRI features to classify 121 lesions from 52 surgical prostate-cancer patients as lower or higher risk against whole-mount pathology. Patient-separated repeated internal validation reported AUC 0.86. Additional models explored recurrence and overall risk in smaller subsets. This pilot does not establish biopsy replacement, external performance or clinical benefit.
organization: Medical University of Vienna; Ludwig Boltzmann Institute Applied Diagnostics

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Whole-mount pathology reference and repeated Monte Carlo validation that kept all lesions from each patient in one partition.
evidence.unknown: External validation and clinical utility remain unestablished; this small surgical cohort, global redundancy filtering and histology-informed lesion localization constrain generalization.
evidence.ai_role: An ensemble of nine random forests combines imaging features to classify pathology-defined lesion risk, with patient-level partitioning.
